```yaml

  - "οὐκ ἦν σοφὸς ὁ ταῦτα εἰπών"
```

```yaml
content: "Some say that by nature doing injustice is good and suffering injustice is bad, but suffering injustice exceeds doing injustice in the bad it brings by more than doing injustice exceeds suffering in good, so that those unable to escape suffering it and gain from doing it find it advantageous to make a compact with one another neither to do nor to suffer injustice, and from this they began to establish laws and covenants and to call the prescription of law lawful and just."
greek_terms: ["τὸ μὲν ἀδικεῖν ἀγαθόν", "τὸ δὲ ἀδικεῖσθαι κακόν", "νόμιμόν τε καὶ δίκαιον"]
```

```yaml
content: "No one, from the earliest heroes whose speeches survive down to the present, has ever genuinely blamed injustice or praised justice for its own inherent power in the soul; all praise and blame have been directed only at the reputations, honors, and rewards that follow from them, without adequately arguing that injustice is the greatest evil the soul can harbor within itself and justice the greatest good."
greek_terms: ["δόξας", "τιμὰς", "δωρεὰς", "αὐτὸ δ' ἑκάτερον τῇ αὑτοῦ δυνάμει", "μέγιστον κακῶν", "μέγιστον ἀγαθόν"]
stance_events:
  - kind: reported
    stephanus_span: "366d-366e"
    source_ref:
      source_path: raw/plato/greek/republic.txt
      stephanus_span: 366d-366e
      start_marker: 366d
      end_marker: 366e
      start_char: 77637
      end_char: 78555
      text_sha256: "f4d2c3a3edcc0b0478757a73d85dd0892016c1ae8051c12009b7c108fae38831"
final_status: left_standing
observation_ids: []
limits: "This is Adeimantus's diagnosis of the entire tradition of praising justice and blaming injustice. It is a report about what no one has done, not a thesis that Socrates has yet addressed. The claim is programmatic for the remainder of the dialogue."
review_status: accepted
```

```yaml

content: "The intelligible realm is divided into two subsections: in one the soul is compelled to investigate from hypotheses, using as images the things imitated by the visible realm, proceeding not to a first principle but to a conclusion; in the other the soul proceeds from hypothesis to an unhypothetical first principle, without images, using forms themselves through themselves."
greek_terms:
  - νοητοῦ
  - ὑποθέσεων
  - ἀρχὴν
  - τελευτήν
  - εἴδεσι
  - ἀνυπόθετον
stance_events:
```

```yaml
claim_id: claim_republic_0557

content: "If the one is always seen together with an opposite so that it appears no more one than the contrary, then the soul is compelled to ask what the one itself is, and the study of the one becomes a conductor and turner toward the contemplation of being."
greek_terms:
  - "τὸ ἕν"
  - "ἐναντίωμα"
  - "οὐσίαν"
  - "ἀγωγῶν"
  - "μεταστρεπτικῶν"
```


```yaml
claim_id: claim_republic_0559

content: "Calculation and arithmetic are, it seems, among the studies sought, because they are conductors toward truth; they are necessary for the warrior on account of battle-order and for the philosopher because he must grasp being by rising out of becoming."

  - "λογιστική"
  - "ἀριθμητική"
  - "ἀγωγὰ πρὸς ἀλήθειαν"
  - "οὐσίας"
```

```yaml

  - "λογιστικήν"
  - "ἰδιωτικῶς"
  - "τῶν ἀριθμῶν φύσεως"
  - "μεταστροφῆς"

  - "οὐσίαν"
```



```yaml

  source_path: raw/plato/greek/republic.txt
  stephanus_span: 561b-561c
  start_marker: 561b
  end_marker: 561c
  start_char: 441137
  end_char: 441991
  text_sha256: "e0a31f999395b5008fc4741d0e9b5623c7d5dd2b344c8af1f6110209b8c3faf4"
speaker: "(unattributed)"
claim_kind: thesis
content: "The democratic man refuses to admit true logos into his inner citadel when it says that some pleasures belong to noble and good desires and others to base ones, and that the former should be pursued and honored while the latter should be chastened and enslaved; instead he claims all pleasures are alike and equally to be honored."
greek_terms: []
stance_events:
  - kind: asserted
    stephanus_span: "561b-561c"
    source_ref:
      source_path: raw/plato/greek/republic.txt
      stephanus_span: 561b-561c
      start_marker: 561b
      end_marker: 561c
      start_char: 441137
      end_char: 441991
      text_sha256: "e0a31f999395b5008fc4741d0e9b5623c7d5dd2b344c8af1f6110209b8c3faf4"
final_status: left_standing
observation_ids: []
limits: "The record reports what the democratic man denies (a distinction among pleasures) and what he asserts (all pleasures alike and equally honorable). It does not assert that the denied logos is true, only that it is a true logos within the dialogue's frame."
review_status: accepted
```

```yaml
content: "Escaping detection when committing injustice makes one still more depraved, whereas in the one who is detected and punished the beastly part is lulled and tamed, the tame part is liberated, and the whole soul, restored to its best nature, acquires a more honorable condition — acquiring temperance and justice together with wisdom — by as much as the soul is more honorable than the body."
greek_terms: []
stance_events:
  - kind: posed_for_examination
    stephanus_span: "591b-591c"
    source_ref:
      source_path: raw/plato/greek/republic.txt
      stephanus_span: 591b-591c
      start_marker: 591b
      end_marker: 591c
      start_char: 500325
      end_char: 501145
      text_sha256: "adfa8b4d078d6f19104ca03cc827abb8441b9fc77231bd2b621d6b77c9fe2164"
final_status: posed_only
observation_ids: []
limits: "Posed as a question ('or does not the one escaping detection become still more depraved...?') and Glaucon answers 'entirely so.' The claim explains why escaping punishment is not profitable — punishment tames the beastly part and liberates the tame part. This directly addresses the earlier challenge (from Republic II) about whether the undetected unjust person fares better."
review_status: rejected
```

